newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China, Indonesia buy Indian-origin soymeal-traders.
newsitem.headline: China, Indonesia buy Indian-origin soymeal-traders.

text.p: China and Indonesia have bought quantities of new crop Indian soymeal for November to January shipment, regional traders said on Monday.
Indonesia purchased around 20,000 to 25,000 tonnes of soymeal for November/December shipment at a price of around $316 a tonne C&F, the traders said.
The volume of purchases by China was not immediately available, but the price being paid by Chinese buyers was around $320-$325 a tonne C&F, Singapore-based traders said.
India had contracted to export nearly 300,000 tonnes of soymeal for November to January shipment, Indian traders said on Friday in Indore.
Of that amount, about 100,000 tonnes was bought by Singapore-based Peter Cremer, 60,000 tonnes by Toepfer International of Germany and 40,000 tonnes by Hong Kong-based Concordia, the traders said.
Details of the other deals were not immediately available.

New crop Indian soymeal is currently quoted at about $280 to $285 a tonne FOB and freight costs to Malaysia and Indonesia would add about $25 a tonne to the shipment, traders said. The freight rate to China was quoted at about $30 a tonne.
Malaysia has not yet bought any meal from India and there was no immediate word on possible purchases by Thailand, they added.
